# Buki

> A Chrome extension that identifies a book from a photograph of its cover, anywhere on
> the web, and files it on a shelf stored in the browser. It reads the picture rather than
> the page text, which is what separates it from every other reading-list tool.

## What it is for

Someone sees a book in a screenshot, a post, a video thumbnail or a photo of a shelf, and
has no title to search for. Every reading tracker begins after you already know the title
and are willing to type it. Buki is upstream of that: it is how you get the title.

## How it works

Right-click any image and choose "Save book to shelf". The picture and the surrounding
text go to a vision model together, because the words beside a cover are often what make a
hard cover legible. The reading is then confirmed against OpenLibrary rather than trusted.
Nothing is saved until the person chooses a pile: Now, Next, Someday or Read. One
photograph can hold several books and each one gets its own decision.

## What makes it different

Three things, and each one is a gap in the existing category:

1. **It reads the picture, not the caption.** Extensions like TBR Bookmarker parse page
   text, so a book that exists only as a photograph is invisible to them.
2. **It works anywhere there is an image.** Phone scanner apps solve the same recognition
   problem but assume the physical book is in your hands, which is useless at 11pm when the
   book is on a screen.
3. **It keeps the page you caught it from.** Google Lens answers "what is this book" and
   then the answer evaporates. Buki keeps the book and the reason you wanted it.

## Pricing

Free forever with no account and no card: ten hosted cover readings, unlimited catches
from a shop link, and the entire shelf kept permanently. Bring your own vision-model API
key and the cover reading is unlimited and free forever.

Buki Pro is $4 per month or $29 per year: unlimited hosted cover reading with no key to
obtain, no throttling, and export to Goodreads and StoryGraph. Cancelling keeps every book
already caught, because the shelf is local data on the user's own machine.

See /pricing.md for a machine-readable version.

## Privacy

There is no account and no sync. The shelf lives in `chrome.storage.local`. The only thing
that leaves the machine is the image the user explicitly asked Buki to identify, sent to
the recognition provider, and the resulting title, sent to OpenLibrary to confirm the book
exists. Source is MIT licensed and public.
